question.leadin: Name these New World Colonies now known by their state names.
question.text: Captain John Smith helped to found Jamestown, a settlement within this colony.
question.clue: A raid on Martin's Hundred by Opechancanough threatened this area.

swap.leadin: The split between "Old Lights" and "New Lights" occurred during this period.
swap.text: Evangelists like George Whitfield and Jonathan Edwards were active during what period of intense religious fervor in early colonial America?
swap.clue: A speech from this movement compares its audience to "a spider, or some loathsome insect" held over a fire.

question.text: In this 1676 war, which included the Great Swamp Fight, a namesake chief fought soldiers and priests from Plymouth and Massachusetts Bay. Native or colonial name acceptable.
question.answerHtml: King Philip’s War [or Metacomet’s War; or Pometacomet’s War; accept “rebellion” in place of “war”]
question.clue: A turning point in this conflict occurred with the Great Swamp Fight, after which the Narragansett were forced to withdraw.

swap.leadin: Give the following about labor practices in 19th century America.
swap.text: Many Europeans migrated to the Americas by becoming this type of laborer, in which they exchanged several years of labor for their passage and were guaranteed their freedom at the end of the contract.
swap.answerHtml: indentured servants (accept word forms, like indentured servitude; prompt on servant)
swap.clue: The book's second chapter argues that the "color line" was created to pacify these people by distinguishing them from slaves. These servants worked without pay for a set amount of time.

question.text: Williams also wrote The Bloody Tenent yet more Bloody after this theologian denounced his ideas in The Bloody Tenent Washed and Made White. This man's daughter and her husband, Increase Mather, named their son after him.
question.clue: This Puritan clergyman who advocated for the right of ministers to preach to their congregations in such works as The Keys to the Kingdom of Heaven and The Way of the Churches of Christ in New England.

swap.leadin: In the "Ballot or the Bullet" speech, Malcolm X says that African-Americans "didn't land on [this object]; [this object] landed on us."
swap.text: Name this object which was split in two before being reunited under a large canopy near a harbor in 1880. The date "1620" is inscribed on this object.
swap.clue: Malcolm X gave a famous speech where he claimed that this entity "landed on us" in reference to the lack of civil rights for African-Americans.

question.leadin: Name some Native American groups outside the Five Nations who spoke Iroquoian languages.
question.text: This tribe joined the Five Nations in 1722 following their namesake war against the British in North Carolina. This group's addition resulted in the modern-day Iroquois League having six nations.
question.answerHtml: Tuscarora [accept Skarure; prompt on hemp gatherers or shirt wearers and equivalent]
question.clue: They threatened to take sides in the struggle between Thomas Cary and Governor Hyde, and ultimately formed alliances with the Nynee and Bear River peoples to prosecute an unsuccessful 1711 to 1713 war against North Carolina.

swap.leadin: William Kieft ("KEEFT") served as a director of this colony.
swap.text: Name this colony led by the peg-legged director-general Peter Stuyvesant ("STYE-vuh-sint"). The Peace of Breda transferred ownership of this colony to the English.
swap.answerHtml: New Netherland [or Nieuw Nederland or New Amsterdam or New Netherlands; reject “Netherlands”]
swap.clue: This colony which fought with the Algonquin in the Peach Tree War while being led by a man with a pegleg.

question.leadin: Name these founders of early American colonies.
question.text: In 1732, this English philanthropist received a charter from George II to settle the colony of Georgia, making it not only a buffer against Spanish invasion but also a refuge for debtors.
question.clue: Earlier, this man led a Parliamentary committee on prison reform, which inspired him to found a haven for debtors.

swap.leadin: Name these conferences of early American history.
swap.text: This 1754 meeting featuring seven of the colonies was convened to negotiate treaties with the Iroquois, but it became better known for the introduction of Benjamin Franklin's Plan of Union.
swap.clue: Peter Wraxall served as its chronicler, repeatedly referencing the "Fire of Friendship".

question.leadin: This man succeeded John Endecott in his first stint as governor.
question.text: Name this governor of the Massachusetts Bay Colony, who envisioned his settlement as a "city upon a hill".
question.clue: He sided with Thomas Dudley and John Endecott in a dispute that led to the banishment of John Wheelwright.

swap.text: With the guidance of Guido Verbeck, Meiji commissioned one of these groups led by and named for Iwakura Tomomi. Another of these groups travelled to San Francisco aboard the western warship Kanrin Maru.
swap.clue: Examples of these structures, 21 of which were connected via a 600-mile path, included San Carlos Borromeo de Carmelo.

question.leadin: At the 1784 Christmas Conference, this denomination officially took up an anti-slavery stance.
question.text: Name this denomination whose "African Episcopal" offshoot, established by Richard Allen and Absalom Jones, is the oldest Protestant denomination founded by African-Americans.
question.answerHtml: Methodism [or Wesleyan Church; or Methodist Episcopal Church; or African Methodist Episcopal Church; prompt on AME Church]
question.clue: "Connexions," or offshoots, of this movement included the Kilhamites.

swap.leadin: During one conflict, John Alderman killed this man as part of a punitive expedition led by Benjamin Church.
swap.text: Name this leader, who met with Mary Rowlandson during her captivity amid a conflict in which John Sassamon's body was found at Assawompset Pond.
swap.clue: He was slain while trying to avoid Benjamin Church's men while hiding in the Miery Swamp near Mount Hope.

question.leadin: The first of these people to use a certain route was a hermit named Pelayo who convinced Bishop Theodemir to excavate a tomb marked by a ray of light in the forests of Iria.
question.text: Name these people who traded and collected scallop shells to pay for provisions. St. Dominic of the Causeway allegedly resurrected one of these people who was framed for theft alongside two chickens.
question.answerHtml: pilgrims [accept synonyms like visitors to a shrine; answers need to specify travelers for religious reasons]
question.clue: Over half of this group died during its first winter in America before they received help from the Wampanoag Indians.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the French and Indian War.
swap.text: This battle on the banks of a river in present-day Western Pensylvania prevented English Major General Edward Braddock from reaching Fort Duquesne and also resulted in Braddock's death.
swap.clue: Daniel de Beaujeu formulated the winning battle plan but died early in this battle, which is sometimes named for the body of water that was crossed in a failed attempt to reach Fort Duquesne ("doo-CANE").

question.leadin: He spent six years as governor of the Louisiana territory before being sent to the Bastille due to political intrigues.
question.text: Name this French explorer who founded Detroit in 1701.
question.answer: Antoine Laumet de La Mothe Cadillac

swap.leadin: Name these things about Anglo-Powhatan relations.
swap.text: This younger brother of Powhatan held effective control of the confederacy for most of the three Anglo-Powhatan wars. His name literally means that he had a white soul.
swap.clue: This man who succeeded his brother as Paramount Chief of the Powhatan. John Smith first encountered Pocahontas after this man captured him and brought him to Werowocomoco (WAIR-uh-woh-KOH-muh-koh).

question.text: De La Warr left this tyrannical deputy of his in charge of Virginia, and then died on a return voyage trying to replace him. This bad-ass once kidnapped Pocahontas, and later commanded an expedition against the French in Algiers.
question.clue: This military leader abducted Pocahantas and held her captive to negotiate with the Powhatan. He later led raids against Acadia and served as governor of the Virginia Colony.

swap.leadin: It included a massacre at Pavonia and lasted from 1643 to 1645.
swap.text: Name this conflict between the colonists of New Netherland and a local Indian group over the imposition of a tax on Indians.
swap.answer: Kieft's War or the Wappinger War
